chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Farsi, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever from my nation is saved from four characteristics will have Paradise: being saved from immersion in the world, following selfish desires, lust of the belly, and lust of the private part. And whoever from the women of my nation is saved from four characteristics will have Paradise: if she guards what is between her legs, obeys her husband, prays her five [daily prayers], and fasts her month [of Ramadan].

key_terms.شَهْوَةُ الْفَرْجِ: Lust of the private part (sexual desire)

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics that lead to Paradise for men and women according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the concept of *al-salamah* (salvation/deliverance) from specific spiritual and physical vices, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both internal purification and external compliance. The narration distinguishes between the general male struggle against worldly attachment (*ghurm*) and base desires (*shahwat*), while outlining a structured path for women centered on chastity (*hifz al-farj*), marital obedience, and the pillars of worship. This dual approach underscores the holistic nature of Islamic ethics, where personal discipline is directly linked to eternal reward.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-54 Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja’far quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saf’far, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Hassan al-Farsi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Hussein ibn Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

Whoever in my nation abandons the following four characteristics shall go to Paradise: getting deeply involved in this world; following selfish desires; lust for food and lust for sex. And whoever from the women in my nation has four characteristics shall go to Paradise: guards her honor; obey her husband; says the five daily prayers; and fasts for the month of Ramazan .”
